response.title: which dehumidifiers work in a cold garage or basement
response.answer:
For a cold garage or basement, you need a dehumidifier specifically rated for low-temperature operation. Many standard household dehumidifiers become inefficient below 60°F (16°C), and their coils can freeze.

The best choice depends on how cold the space gets.

Important: A compressor dehumidifier rated down to 41°F may technically operate at that temperature, but it will typically remove much less moisture than its advertised daily capacity.

markup:
For a **cold garage or basement**, you need a dehumidifier specifically rated for low-temperature operation. Many standard household dehumidifiers become inefficient below 60°F (16°C), and their coils can freeze.

The best choice depends on how cold the space gets.

## Which type works at which temperature?

| Garage/basement temperature | Best type |
|---|---|
| 60–80°F (16–27°C) | Standard compressor dehumidifier |
| 41–60°F (5–16°C) | Low-temperature compressor with automatic defrost |
| 33–40°F (1–4°C) | Desiccant dehumidifier, or a specialty low-temperature unit |
| Below 32°F (0°C) | Desiccant system specifically rated for freezing conditions |

**Important:** A compressor dehumidifier rated down to 41°F may technically operate at that temperature, but it will typically remove much less moisture than its advertised daily capacity.
